items.statement: The five EQ-5D-5L items form a strong Mokken scale. The level sum score can therefore order respondents along a latent health variable, with higher scores indicating poorer health.

Item ordering gives an interpretation of the level sum score. Pain and anxiety/depression characterize the lower range, mobility and usual activities add at the middle range, and self-care limitations occur at the middle-to-higher range.

For applications that require strong scalability or item ordering, researchers could calculate the level sum score from the four physical items and assess anxiety/depression separately. The choice depends on the population and application.
The level sum score is a simple scoring approach that is independent of population-specific value sets and can support international comparisons. It can be less informative in healthy populations.

The dataset included only adults from Western, developed countries. The findings might not extend to other populations if interpretations of item descriptions and response categories affect person and item ordering.
The data came from online survey panels, whose participants can differ from the general population.
The analysis did not include children. The authors stated that similar research is needed in children and adolescents.

items.label: EQ-5D-5L level sum score as a non-preference-based summary score
items.description: The score ranges from 5 to 25. It assigns values from 1 to 5 to the five EQ-5D-5L response levels and adds the values across dimensions. It does not use population-specific preference weights.

items.label: Tension between multidimensional health and a single latent health construct
items.description: The EQ-5D-5L covers distinct physical and mental health dimensions, while item-response approaches assume that items indicate one latent variable.
